$why: Moved out of claude.sh on 2026-08-16. THE WRITER PROMPT -- the one the whole pipeline exists
to send, and the last and largest to leave the script.
Twenty-six of its sections were command substitutions, each carrying its own HEADING inside
the substitution: reviewer feedback, verification criteria, codeline facts, test criteria,
dependency contracts, cross-codeline contracts, the brownfield policy. The words the writer
reads were assembled by shell conditionals spread over sixty lines and could not be read as a
prompt anywhere. The caller composes each section and passes it.
VERIFIED BY RECONSTRUCTION rather than by execution. Several sections shell out to jq against
the real PRD, so running the original with sample values proves nothing. Substituting every
placeholder back and requiring byte equality with the heredoc proves what is actually at risk:
that nothing was dropped, reordered or reworded. What the substitutions evaluate to is
unchanged, because the caller passes the same expressions.
description: The implementation prompt sent to the story writer.
body:
__SPEC_REALITY_WARNING____WRITE_FIRST_DIRECTIVE__

__WRITE_FIRST_LINES__
---

Implement user story __STORY_ID__: __TITLE__

## Story Description
__DESCRIPTION__

## Acceptance Criteria
__STRING_INVARIANTS_BLOCK__
__AGENT_INPUTS__
__REVIEW_FEEDBACK__
__SKILL_NOTE_BLOCK__
__VERIFICATION_CRITERIA__
__CODELINE_FACTS_BLOCK__
__PROJECT_TOOLS_BLOCK__
__TEST_OWNERSHIP_BLOCK__
__CODEGRAPH_TOOL_BLOCK__
__UNCOVERED_VC_BLOCK__
__BROWNFIELD_TEST_POLICY__
__NEW_DEPENDENCY_DIRECTIVE__
__TC_FACTS__
__TC_MOCK_STRATEGY__
__TC_BANNED__

## Technical Notes
__TECHNICAL_NOTES__
__EXISTING_FILE_CONTENTS__

## Files to Create/Modify (EXACT ABSOLUTE PATHS — start here; this list is not exhaustive)
These are the files the analysis identified. Use these exact paths for them. The list is a
STARTING POINT, not a fence: it is derived from the ticket and may be incomplete or may name
a path this repository spells differently. If your change genuinely requires another file in
this repository, write it — the only files closed to you are ones another story OWNS, and
attempting one of those returns a specific refusal saying so. Do NOT work around a refusal by
repeatedly rewriting a file you can already write; that is never the fix. When you write a
file that is not listed here, say which file and why in your final message, so the reviewer
sees the whole change.
__FILES__

## Dependencies
__DEPENDENCIES__
__DEPENDENCY_CONTRACTS__
__MODULE_RESOLUTION__
__CROSS_CODELINE_CONTRACT__

## Instructions
__WRITE_FIRST_DIRECTIVE__
__WRITE_FIRST_LINES_2__
__CONDITIONAL_SECTION__

__CONDITIONAL_SECTION_2__
2. Implement all acceptance criteria for this story
__TC_FACTS_2__
4. Do NOT create tests unless explicitly required in acceptance criteria

After implementation, provide a brief summary of what was created/modified.
$mayBeEmptyWhy: Each is a section build_implementation_prompt initialises empty and fills only on a condition, so absent is a REAL state: no prior review (every first attempt), no persisted skill notes, no codegraph plugin, a greenfield file, a single codeline, a non-brownfield run, all VCs covered. Without this the engine-prompt empty-payload guard (added 5f3995f, 2026-08-23) refused every writer prompt: review_feedback is empty unless review-feedback-<story>.json exists, which it cannot on a first attempt, so build_implementation_prompt returned 1 and claude.sh logged 'REFUSED — not invoking the writer' for EVERY story. The list is derived by executing the real builder against a realistic story and recording what it left empty, not chosen by hand. A second pass against the real MOCK3-1 story added __WRITE_FIRST_LINES__, __VERIFICATION_CRITERIA__, __FILES__ and __WRITE_FIRST_LINES_2__: a story that declares no verification criteria and no files is a real state the PRD produces today, and the write-first lines are conditional on it.
$mayBeEmptyReview: Two entries deserve a second look when anyone next touches this: __AGENT_INPUTS__ (empty may mean 'this role declares no inputs' OR that the agent-inputs lookup returned nothing) and __TEST_OWNERSHIP_BLOCK__ (empty on non-brownfield runs, and test ownership is a policy the operator has been explicit about). Both are listed because production genuinely emits them empty today; neither should be treated as settled.
$whyFilesIsNotOptional: __FILES__ was briefly listed here and is deliberately NOT. A live haiku call on 2026-08-26 was given a writer prompt with no files and answered: 'I need clarification on the file paths ... the working directory is empty. Could you provide the actual absolute file paths?' A writer with nowhere to write cannot act, so an empty __FILES__ must REFUSE rather than render. The story that produced it (MOCK3-1) was PRE-SPEC — canonical stories carry no technicalNotes, and the spec pass adds them before the writer runs — so refusing here also catches the real defect of invoking the writer before elaboration.
